author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Como moddear juegos de PS2 (PCSX2 debugger + pnach)
summary: RubioDev records an extended Spanish workshop on creating PCSX2 PNACH modifications with the debugger, preserving the exploratory address-search process and linking a dedicated format reference instead of presenting only a finished code.

blocks.text: The eighty-six-minute length allows viewers to watch uncertainty, failed assumptions and eventual progress while the creator learns to modify PS2 software in personal spare time. PCSX2’s debugger supplies runtime memory observations, and a linked SlyMods reference explains the PNACH file syntax used to turn a discovered change into a repeatable patch. That connection between investigation and a documented text format is more transferable than copying one address: it shows how a result can be recorded, annotated and tested again.

The author describes this as a developing hobby, not a definitive debugging course. An address found in one Tenchu revision may move in another region, executable build or game state, and a working write can still damage progress or hide an emulator bug. Use lawful personal software, back up memory cards, identify the CRC and restart repeatedly before trusting a condition. Do not carry modifications into competitive or online contexts. The stream teaches a research path; current PNACH syntax and debugger behavior should be confirmed in maintained documentation.
